To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the well-founded semantics is a natural semantics for general logic programming, that the well-founded model of a program can be viewed as a “unique stable model”, and that the well-founded partial models are the “least” partial models.
the well-founded semantics is a generalization of the stable semantics, and that a program has at least one stable model if and only if it is well-behaved.

(i) the well-founded semantics is a well-defined semantics of programs in which negation is allowed in the body of rules, (ii) it is a conservative extension of previous semantics for programs without negation in the body of the rules, and (iii) it is the only semantics for programs that is both conservative and well-defined.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the declarative semantics of general logic programs,
defining a declarative semantics for general logic programming that is more general than previously defined semantics.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a well-behaved program has a well-founded semantics, and a program has a stable model if it is well-behaved.
the well-founded model of a program, if it exists, is the unique stable model of the program.
the well-founded semantics is the “correct” semantics for general logic programming, and the stable models are the “unique” models of general logic programming, but the two are not identical.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the well-founded semantics provides a generalization of the stable models semantics, while the stable models semantics provides a generaliztion of the well-founded semantics.
we have defined a declarative semantics for general logic programming that properly generalizes previous semantics and that is closely related to Gelfand and Lifechitz’s stable model semantics.
we have defined a semantics for general logic databases that is a generalization of the semantics for stratified logic databases and that is a special case of the semantics of stable logic databases.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the class of programs with unique stable models is properly contained in the larger class of well-behave programs, and that the well-founded model is a natural and useful extension of the stable model to programs that are not well-behaved.
well-founded semantics is a natural and intuitive semantics for general logic programming, and is the appropriate semantics when one wants to associate a single Herbrand model with the program.
we have provided a simple, natural, and general definition of the well-founded semantics, that is a generalization of the well-known stratified and locally stratified semantics.
